title: You already program: what engineering adds
summary: If you build by describing things to an AI agent, you are already programming: you decide the input, the rule and the output. Drake's point is that programming and engineering are different from typing code. Engineering adds one habit: saying how you will know you got it. I can run a tiny Omega program that turns a plain request into a program, and show the compiler refusing a loosely written version instead of guessing.
goal: See that precise description is programming, and that engineering adds a way to know you got it.
key_steps: Name the input, the rule and the output in one sentence
Where your sentence has two readings, pick one out loud
Pick one input where you already know the answer
Run it and compare with what you expected
Treat a refusal from the compiler as a request to be precise

example.code:
note todo: print every input line that starts with TODO, then how many there were
note exit 0 done, 2 the input could not be read
text KW "TODO\nfound \n TODO line(s)\n\n"
note helpers: read all of stdin into inb, walk lines, compare a line prefix with the n-th
note entry of the newline separated table KW, and write table entries, input bytes and numbers
global inb uchar 65536
global num uchar 24
fn rdall to long
t = ulong 0
while lt t len inb bound 65536
k = read 0 inb t sub len inb t
if lt k 0
ret k
end
if eq k 0
ret long t
end
t = add t ulong k
end
ret neg long 27
end
fn eol s ulong n ulong to ulong
i = s
while lt i n bound 65536
if eq get inb i 10
ret i
end
i = add i 1
end
ret n
end
fn kstart k ulong to ulong
p = ulong 0
c = ulong 0
while lt c k bound 4096
if eq get KW p 10
c = add c 1
end
p = add p 1
end
ret p
end
fn klen k ulong to ulong
s = kstart k
i = s
while ne get KW i 10 bound 4096
i = add i 1
end
ret sub i s
end
fn pmat at ulong e ulong k ulong to bool
o = kstart k
m = klen k
if gt m sub e at
ret false
end
for j ulong m
if ne get inb add at j get KW add o j
ret false
end
end
ret true
end
fn emitk o ulong n ulong to void
d = ulong 0
while lt d n bound 4096
w = write 1 KW add o d sub n d
if le w 0
trap 9
end
d = add d ulong w
end
end
fn emiti o ulong n ulong to void
d = ulong 0
while lt d n bound 65536
w = write 1 inb add o d sub n d
if le w 0
trap 9
end
d = add d ulong w
end
end
fn emitn o ulong n ulong to void
d = ulong 0
while lt d n bound 24
w = write 1 num add o d sub n d
if le w 0
trap 9
end
d = add d ulong w
end
end
fn say k ulong to void
emitk kstart k add klen k 1
end
fn word k ulong to void
emitk kstart k klen k
end
fn emitu v ulong to void
p = ulong 24
x = v
while true bound 21
p = sub p 1
put num p uchar add rem x 10 48
x = div x 10
if eq x 0
break
end
end
emitn p sub 24 p
end
fn main to int
r = rdall
if lt r 0
ret 2
end
n = ulong r
s = ulong 0
c = ulong 0
while lt s n bound 65536
e = eol s n
if pmat s e 0
c = add c 1
emiti s sub e s
say 3
end
s = add e 1
end
word 1
emitu c
say 2
ret 0
end

ALL EXIT STATUSES AS EXPECTED

common_mistake: Thinking that because you do not write code, you are not responsible for what it does. Only you know whether you meant 'starts with TODO' or 'mentions TODO'. Fix: state the rule with no wiggle room and check one input whose answer you know.
evidence_note: The example compiled and ran on a Linux ARM64 computer (no GPU) and its output is recorded byte for byte, including a negative control. Rests on the recorded run: todo.om compiled (rc=0) and printed the two lines that start with TODO; the loosely written vague.om was refused with rc=11 (error 11, a bare number with no type). NOT done: nothing here measures learning outcomes.
